description.value: A randomized controlled trial investigating whether mindfulness-based relapse prevention enhances real-time fMRI neurofeedback for reducing alcohol cue-reactivity in patients with Alcohol Use Disorder.

spans.text: In this project we assess the efficacy of regulating cue-reactivity by means of rtfMRI NFB in AUD patients and investigate the impact of MBRP on the NFB procedure and the clinical outcome.

value: We expect that the group receiving the combination treatment (real rtfMRI and MBRP) will profit most in terms of the outcome.
we assume a decreased amount of heavy drinking days and a decreased sum of alcohol consumption.
